title: Maximize Active Section with Trade II
summary: Given a binary string s, you can perform at most one trade to maximize the number of active sections.
statement: Given a binary string s, you can perform at most one trade to maximize the number of active sections. A trade involves converting a block of '1's surrounded by '0's to '0's, and converting a block of '0's surrounded by '1's to '1's. For each query defined by a substring s[li...ri], determine the maximum possible number of active sections after the trade. Return an array of results for each query, treating the substring as if it were surrounded by '1's at both ends.
constraints: s is a nonempty binary string and each query is an inclusive substring range.
For each query, trade only within that substring as though it were surrounded by ones; positions outside remain unchanged.
Return the maximum total active count in the whole string after at most one query-local trade.
hints: A query gain is the best sum of two zero runs separated by one-runs, with its first and last zero runs clipped at query boundaries.
Precompute zero runs, adjacent-run sums, and a sparse table for fully contained interior pairs.
For each range, combine the best interior pair with the few boundary pair configurations, then add the unchanged global active count.
Every eligible pair is either wholly interior or touches a clipped boundary, so the constant set of cases plus RMQ is complete.
editorial: Every eligible pair is either wholly interior or touches a clipped boundary, so the constant set of cases plus RMQ is complete.

tests.explanation: The query cannot improve the string, so the answer is one.
The full range can activate all five positions, while the shorter range uses its clipped boundary zero runs.
